items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Eddie Bert said to me, “you know why we swing? Because we used to play for dancers.

ctx.x: I think metronomes are really important. Most singers hate them. Most musicians don’t like them because they’ve got this ugly click-click. But that’s — I tell them, I explain to them I say, “a long time ago metronomes were these big clumsy things that you’d wind up. Then they made them so you could plug them in the wall. Now they make them really small. So buy the smallest one you can, put fresh batteries in it, and swallow it. That way © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

you’ll always have good time.” Because time is what makes it happen. I mean I don’t want to hear somebody out of tune, but I’d rather hear them out of tune than out of time. Because if you’re in time at least there’s a groove. I mean I don’t want to hear out of tune either, but time, to me — I’ve been really fortunate in being around some musicians that I was buying their LPs when I was a kid. items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Bill Finnegan, Eddie Bert, people that you interviewed that I watched the interviews and listened. I just felt like wow, I was inspired by them and by being able to partake in what they were doing.

ctx.x: We’re back. Okay. Okay so I’ll just pick up. What inspired you to move from the construction business into the music world?

Well when I went up there I was going to stay for a year and a year started to go by and I liked living up there. I left one year and went to work in Washington State in construction. I got to sit in a little bit in a couple of places in Olympia and Seattle. I went back to Alaska. I went to Arizona for a season and worked on a road job. Went back to Alaska. Came back to the East Coast for about eight or nine months, went back to Alaska. There was something about it. I mean there’s two things that’ll happen to you…

performing headliners, one was Sarah Vaughan and one was Steve Allen. Yeah. I said wow. And it was a two week festival. And it wasn’t just performances. It was workshops that you could attend. And these workshops were from square dancing to photography to charcoal drawing to classical violin, singing, dancing, you name it. Arts festival. And they had to two week cabaret class. Not my thing but the instructor was a woman by the name of Chris Calloway. Cab’s daughter. Well that was enough for me to sign up. Cab…
